subject.title: fix(update): prevent compatible plugins from being skipped after npm-global upgrades

question: Is the disclosed Windows proof—real npm-global replacement and convergence followed by separate restart, RPC-health, and discovery checks using a synthesized target bundle—sufficient for this update-path compatibility change, or is one uninterrupted run from an exact PR-head artifact required?
rationale: The code and focused regression coverage support the fix, but repository policy leaves the merge threshold for this compatibility-sensitive production lifecycle to maintainer judgment because the demonstrated artifact and process were not exact and uninterrupted.

options.title: Accept Disclosed Proof
options.body: Treat the observed replacement, convergence, restart, RPC health, and retained-plugin discovery as sufficient despite the clearly documented split lifecycle and synthesized bundle.

options.title: Require Exact-Head Lifecycle
options.body: Hold merge until one uninterrupted managed-service update succeeds using an artifact built entirely from the current PR head.

recommendation.title: Accept Disclosed Proof
recommendation.body: Treat the observed replacement, convergence, restart, RPC health, and retained-plugin discovery as sufficient despite the clearly documented split lifecycle and synthesized bundle.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged downgrade work established the compatibility invariant being extended, making them the strongest available history-based routing candidate for the proof threshold.
